message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1968 | **Night of the Living Dead** (George A. Romero) | The original zombie film that defined a genre. |
| 1974 | **The Exorcist** | A chilling story of demonic possession that still feels fresh. |
| 1978 | **Halloween** (John Carpenter) | The quintessential slasher with a memorable score. |
| 1980 | **The Shining** (Stanley Kubrick) | A haunting psychological thriller set in an isolated hotel. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** | Freddy Krueger’s dream‑based terror is iconic. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | A tense psychological thriller with unforgettable characters. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** | A twisty supernatural thriller that keeps you guessing. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | A fast‑moving, post‑apocalyptic horror that revitalized the zombie genre. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | A gritty, puzzle‑based horror that sparked a long-running franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Low‑budget found‑footage horror that made a huge impact. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** | A modern supernatural horror that blends scares with a strong narrative. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and frightening. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | A unique, slow‑burn horror with a creepy, relentless stalker. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | A slow‑burn, atmospheric horror set in 17th‑century New England. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | A smart, socially conscious horror that blends satire with terror. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | A tense, sound‑driven horror that keeps you on edge. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** | A daylight horror that’s as unsettling as it is beautiful. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** | A modern retelling of a classic tale with strong feminist themes. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** | A supernatural horror that revisits a powerful urban legend. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** | A chilling, supernatural thriller with a unique premise. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** | A horror‑comedy about a murderous AI doll that’s both funny and scary. |

Feel free to pick based on your taste—whether you prefer psychological dread, supernatural chills, or slasher thrills. Enjoy the fright!
